title: How to see word count in Google Docs on Mac: menu, shortcut and live count
metaTitle: How to See Word Count in Google Docs on Mac
description: Learn how to see word count in google docs on mac: open Tools > Word count, use ⌘+Shift+C, or turn on a live count while you type.

intro: To see word count in Google Docs on Mac, open your document in the browser and choose Tools > Word count, or press ⌘+Shift+C. The dialog lists pages, words, characters and characters without spaces, and it covers only highlighted text when you select some first.
tldr: Open Tools > Word count, or press ⌘+Shift+C, while the document has focus.
The dialog shows pages, words, characters and characters without spaces.
Tick Display word count while typing to keep a live count in the bottom-left corner.
Highlight text before you open the dialog to count only that section.
Google's help says headers, footers and footnotes are left out of the total.

blocks.text: Open word count from the Tools menu

The word count option lives under Tools, in the menu row near the top of the page. That row sits just below the document name and reads File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, Tools and so on. Google's help page gives the same path: Tools, then Word count, then Done to close the window. It is the most reliable route when you are new to the app.

items: Find the menu row just below the document name.
Click Tools. The menu drops down from there.
Choose Word count. The dialog opens over the page.
Click Done when you finish reading the numbers.

blocks.text: Use the keyboard shortcut ⌘+Shift+C

Google's keyboard shortcut page lists Word count as ⌘+Shift+C on Mac. On Windows and Chrome OS the same action is Ctrl+Shift+C. The shortcut needs the document to have focus, so click into the text first. If your cursor is in the address bar or a comment box, the keys go there instead. For repeat checks mid-draft, the shortcut is quicker than the menu.

blocks.title: Chrome may catch the keys
blocks.text: Chrome's DevTools shortcut page lists ⌘+Shift+C as the key that toggles Inspect Element mode. If an inspector panel opens instead of the dialog, the keys reached Chrome, not Docs. Click back in the document body and try again, or use Tools > Word count.
Read the four numbers in the dialog

The dialog shows four counts. Pages tells you how many pages the document runs. Words counts each word. Characters counts every character, including spaces. Characters without spaces leaves the spaces out. Most word limits use Words. Some title fields and social posts use characters, so read the label before you trust a number.
Turn on the live word count while you type

If you want the number on screen all the time, open Word count and tick Display word count while typing. Click OK. The count appears in the bottom-left corner of the window and keeps updating as you type. To hide it, click the count box and choose Hide word count. You can turn it back on from Tools > Word count.

blocks.text: Count only the words you select

Highlight the text before you open the dialog. Google's help says that when you select a section, the word count applies to that section only. This is the fastest way to check one paragraph, a quote or a conclusion. Click once in the body text to clear the selection before you check the whole document. A selection left over from earlier is a common reason for a small, surprising number.
Worked example: checking a word limit

Say an assignment caps the essay at a set number of words, and you are unsure whether the conclusion runs too long. Open Word count and note the whole-document Words figure. Then highlight only the conclusion and open Word count again. The second Words figure tells you how long the conclusion runs. Subtract it from the total to see how much room the rest of the essay has.

Keep the live count on while you cut and add sentences. You can watch the total move without reopening the dialog each time. When you get close to the limit, switch to the selection method for the sections you changed.
What the count leaves out

Google's help says that unless you select a section, word count applies to everything except headers, footers and footnotes. Headers and footers are the running text at the top and bottom of each page. Footnote text does not add to the total. If your rules count those parts, you need a separate check.

blocks.title: Footnotes: follow Google's help
blocks.text: Some third-party guides say footnotes are counted. Google's help page says they are not. Follow Google's page. If your rules include footnotes, copy them into a separate document and count that document on its own.
Size limits on long documents

Google's Drive help page says a Google Docs document can hold up to 1.02 million characters. Most essays, reports and book chapters sit far below that line. The same help page says a text file converted to Google Docs format can be up to 50 MB. If a long import fails, split the file into smaller parts and convert each part on its own.
Screen reader users and the spoken count

If you use a screen reader, Google's keyboard shortcut page lists a separate combination for reading the word count aloud. Hold Ctrl and ⌘, press A, then press W. It does a different job from the dialog. Use it when you want the number spoken to you instead of shown on screen.
Mistakes people make with word count

items: Counting the whole document when only one section matters. Highlight first, or clear the selection.
Reading Pages as a word total. Pages counts pages, not words.
Ignoring footnotes and headers when the rules include them. Check the rules before you rely on the total.
Pressing ⌘+Shift+C while Chrome has focus. You get an inspector instead of the dialog.
Using Words when the limit is set in characters. Read the label before you copy the number.

blocks.text: Ask Lazur where the count lives

If the menu looks different on your Mac, or you want a second set of eyes, hold ⌥⌘ (Option and Command) and ask Lazur where the word count option is. Lazur looks at your screen only while you hold the keys. It draws a circle and a label around the item it means, then answers out loud.

Ask Lazur to walk you through the dialog instead, and it guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on. Lazur does not click for you. Audio and the screenshot are sent to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.
Word count on a phone or tablet

The mobile app uses a different path. Tap the More icon in the top-right corner, then tap Word Count. To count a selection, highlight the text first, then tap More and Word Count. PCWorld's guide from 2022 says live counting was not available on mobile at the time. Check the current app before you rely on that.
Why counts differ between tools

A number from Google Docs and a number from another editor can disagree. Each tool has its own rules for what a word is, and each may treat headers, footers and notes differently. Match the tool your rules name. If you must switch, run the count in the tool you will submit from.
What to do next

Once the count is right, the next job is often formatting. For page numbers on a printed draft, see [how to add page numbers in Google Docs on Mac](/how-to/add-page-numbers-in-google-docs). If a reviewer has left suggestions, [how to accept or reject suggestions in Google Docs on Mac](/how-to/accept-or-reject-suggestions-in-google-docs) shows the next step.

faq.question: Where is word count in Google Docs on Mac?
faq.answer: Open the document in your browser, click Tools in the menu row, and choose Word count. You can also press ⌘+Shift+C while the document has focus. The dialog shows pages, words, characters and characters without spaces.

faq.question: Does word count in Google Docs include footnotes?
faq.answer: According to Google's help page, no. Unless you select a section, the count covers everything except headers, footers and footnotes. Some third-party guides say footnotes are counted, so follow Google's page and check your own rules.

faq.question: Can I see the word count while I type?
faq.answer: Yes. Open Tools > Word count, tick Display word count while typing, then click OK. The live count sits in the bottom-left corner. Click that box and choose Hide word count to turn it off.

faq.question: How do I count words in only one part of a document?
faq.answer: Highlight the text first, then open Word count from the menu or with ⌘+Shift+C. The dialog counts only the highlighted section. Click once in the body text afterward to clear the selection.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: This guide could not confirm a native Google Docs app for Mac, so the steps assume the browser version. Check Google's help center if you want to be sure which options exist.

faq.question: Is the shortcut the same on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Google's keyboard shortcut page lists Ctrl+Shift+C for Word count on Windows and Chrome OS. On a Mac the same action uses ⌘ in place of Ctrl.

faq.question: Does Lazur count my words for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Google Docs for you. It can point at Tools > Word count, draw a circle around it, and walk you through the dialog one click at a time. Lazur runs on macOS only, and Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Why does my count look too low?
faq.answer: The most common reason is a highlighted selection left over from earlier. Click once in the body text and check again. Headers, footers and footnotes sit outside the total, so a shorter count can be correct.

How to check your word count in Google Docs

task: See word count in Google Docs on Mac

steps.name: Open the document in your browser
steps.text: Open the Google Doc in a browser on your Mac. Click inside the body text so the cursor sits in the document. The keyboard shortcut needs the document to have focus.
steps.tip: If the cursor is in the address bar, click back into the page before you press the keys.

steps.name: Open the Tools menu
steps.text: Look at the menu row just below the document name. It reads File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, Tools and so on. Click Tools to open the list.
steps.tip: If Tools is missing or greyed out, you may have view-only access. Ask the owner for edit or comment access.

steps.name: Choose Word count
steps.text: Click Word count in the list. The dialog opens over the page. You can skip the menu by pressing ⌘+Shift+C while the document has focus.
steps.tip: Chrome's DevTools use the same keys. If an inspector panel opens, click back in the document and try again.

steps.name: Read the four counts
steps.text: Read Pages, Words, Characters and Characters without spaces. Words is the number most word limits use. Click Done to close the dialog.
steps.tip: Pages counts pages, not words. Do not use it as a word target.

steps.name: Turn on the live count (optional)
steps.text: Tick Display word count while typing, then click OK. The count sits in the bottom-left corner and updates as you type.
steps.tip: To hide it, click the count box and choose Hide word count.

steps.name: Count only a highlighted section
steps.text: Highlight the paragraph or section you need. Open Word count with the menu or the shortcut. The dialog counts only the highlighted text.
steps.tip: Click once in the body text to clear the selection before you check the whole document.

shortcuts.action: Screen reader: read word count aloud
shortcuts.keys: Hold Ctrl+⌘, press A, then W

troubleshooting.problem: Shortcut opens an inspector panel instead of the dialog
troubleshooting.fix: Chrome's DevTools use ⌘+Shift+C for Inspect Element, so the keys reached Chrome, not Docs. Click in the document body and try again. If it still does nothing, check your Chrome extensions and any managed-device policy, or use Tools > Word count.

troubleshooting.problem: The Words number is much lower than expected
troubleshooting.fix: Text is probably still highlighted. Click once in the body to clear the selection, then reopen Word count. Headers, footers and footnotes are also left out of the total.

troubleshooting.problem: The live count does not appear
troubleshooting.fix: Open Tools > Word count and check that Display word count while typing is ticked. Click OK. If the box still does not show, reload the browser tab.

troubleshooting.problem: Tools menu is missing or greyed out
troubleshooting.fix: You may have view-only access. Ask the document owner for edit or comment access, then reload the page.

troubleshooting.problem: The document will not take more text
troubleshooting.fix: Google's Drive help says a Google Docs document can hold up to 1.02 million characters. Split long files into parts, and count each part on its own.

troubleshooting.problem: The total does not match the rules you were given
troubleshooting.fix: Check which field the rules use. Pages, Words and Characters are different numbers. Headers, footers and footnotes sit outside the total, so count them separately if the rules include them.
